observation.visible_scene: A calm pond or slow stream in a hilly valley under a clear blue sky. A large leafless tree grows directly out of the water at center, its trunk and bare branches mirrored on the surface. Dry golden reeds/grass line the near bank in the foreground; brown grassy hills close in on the left and right, and a faint snow-dusted ridge sits in the background left. The water is mostly glassy with a few soft ripples.
visible_changes: The reflections in the water (the dark trunk column, the squiggly reflection of the left-reaching branches, the bright sky patch, and the dark hill reflection on the right) continuously deform, wiggle, and shift shape frame to frame, indicating gentle motion of the water surface (small ripples).

The actual tree, its bare branches, the foreground grass, the hills, and the background ridge keep the same positions and shapes relative to the frame edges from t=0.000 to t=2.669, i.e. no object translation and no camera pan/zoom are evident.
A thin ripple line on the right side of the water surface moves slightly in position and intensity across the excerpt.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the ripples are caused by wind or an unseen disturbance, and whether they grow, fade, or persist after the segment ends.
Any motion of the bare twigs outside this window (a possible breeze is not confirmable here).
uncertain_details: Whether the topmost thin twigs sway by a sub-pixel amount; the apparent differences are within the noise of the reflection and cannot be confirmed as branch motion.
The exact framing is static to the eye, but a very small camera drift cannot be fully excluded from these samples.
